summary: This sermon explores two parables from Matthew 13 that describe the kingdom of heaven as small, hidden beginnings that grow into unstoppable, transformative power. Using the images of a mustard seed (an invasive plant no farmer would plant) and leaven (yeast hidden in flour), Jesus reveals that God's kingdom doesn't arrive through worldly power or respectability but spreads quietly, disruptively, and inevitably through faithful obedience.
key_points: The mustard seed represents the wild, invasive, uncontrollable nature of God's kingdom—small but unstoppable once planted
The kingdom is not safe or domesticated; it disrupts expectations and spreads beyond human control
Leaven illustrates how the kingdom works hidden but thoroughly, transforming everything it touches from the inside out
Believers must test all 'leaven' against Jesus' teachings, as false teaching can also spread quietly
Faithfulness in small, hidden acts of obedience matters—God works beneath the surface in ways we cannot see
big_idea: The kingdom of heaven begins as something small and hidden that the world overlooks, but once planted it grows with wild, disruptive, unstoppable power that transforms everything from the inside out.
title: PARABLES: Small Beginnings, Big Power
